chunks: Thirty-three - Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id said: Ahmad ibn Yousuf narrated to us, saying: Isma'il ibn Mihran narrated to us, from al-Hasan ibn Ali, from his father and Wahb, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah, regarding His saying:

For each [religious following] is a direction toward which it turns. So race to [all that is] good. Wherever you may be, Allah will bring you forth all together. Indeed, Allah is over all things competent.
He said: It was revealed concerning al-Qa'im and his companions; they will gather together without a pre-arranged appointment.

key_terms.الْقَائِم: The Awakened One, a title for the Twelfth Imam
key_terms.غَيْرِ مِيعَادٍ: Without a pre-arranged appointment or fixed time

ai.seo_question: Who does the verse 'So race to good' refer to in Shia interpretation?
ai.summary: In al-Nu'mani’s *Kitab al-Ghayba*, this narration interprets the verse 'For each is a direction to which he turns' (2:148) as a specific reference to al-Qa'im and his companions, emphasizing their unique spiritual orientation. It highlights the eschatological reality that their gathering will occur spontaneously ('on non-agreed times') rather than through a fixed, pre-announced schedule, underscoring the element of divine surprise in the Mahdi's reappearance. This view is significant in Shia scholarship for distinguishing the Imam's gathering from general resurrection events.

en.abdullah-al-shahin: (37) Ahmad bin Muhammad bin Sa’eed narrated from Ahmad bin Yousuf from Issma’eel bin Mihran from al-Hasan bin Ali from his father and Wuhayb from Abu Baseer that Abu Abdullah as-Sadiq (as) had said about this verse, “
…therefore hasten to (do) good works; wherever you are, Allah will bring you all together:
” “It has been revealed about al-Qa’im (as) and his companions. They will meet together without an appointment.”
